---
title: "Highlights"
---

Select any sentence on this page and a **Highlight** button appears; click it and the passage
is marked. The mark is the reader's own, stored in their browser and anchored to the block's
content hash, so it is exact and survives a re-render. Click a highlight again to remove it.

This paragraph contains some **bold words** and an [inline link](https://example.com) so that a
highlight stretching across them must wrap several text nodes and still read as one continuous
mark. The robustness of that is the whole point: a reader's emphasis should land exactly where
they put it.

A reader marks the line that matters and finds it again later. That is the most-loved feature
of every e-reader, and a plain web page cannot do it well, because it has no stable handle on
its own content. qmd-fast does: every block already carries a content-derived id.

Math like $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$ and a code listing should be left alone by the highlighter, since
their text is either duplicated for accessibility or structured for syntax colour:

```python
def mark(text: str) -> str:
    return f"<mark>{text}</mark>"
```

Only prose is highlightable in this first version. The marked text reads warm in the light
theme, soft in the dark theme, and gentle in sepia, because the highlight colour is a theme
variable rather than a fixed yellow.
